what: the first stage (the core on four languages, the probes, the migration measure) and the second (interface version 2 and the shared REFERENCE page)

digest.part: Stage 1 (the core on four languages, the two probes, the migration measure, the REFERENCE anatomy) and stage 2 (interface version 2 with the root quick start, the shared REFERENCE page, the rust and elixir ports, the anatomy of the other README families, and the two independent checks). Records read: brief.md, stage1.md, brief2.md, brief3.md, results/s2-restanatomy.txt, s2-v2.txt, s2-check_v2.txt, s2-ref.txt, s2-probe_ref.txt, s2-check_ref.txt. None was missing.

rounds.purpose: Build the core of the write-once structure and test it on the README quick start for ts, go, py and c.
rounds.produced: A resolved SdkDescription per target (sdkdesc.ts), a language-neutral example representation (7 statement kinds, 6 expression kinds), a shared ReadmeQuick.ts, four syntax providers Syntax_ts/go/py/c; the four ReadmeQuick_<lang> deleted; 19 model variations with a reason-tagging diff; lanes; metrics; an H5 probe of doctor and target add.
rounds.changed: Found and fixed a c getenv-without-stdlib.h defect. Decided go prints steps rather than one program, js left unported, a project's own ReadmeQuick_<lang> wins over the provider. Showed source grows for four languages (H2 refuted for this section) and that doctor needs a retired-component rule (H5 open).

rounds.purpose: Independently reproduce the architect's numbers and claims.
rounds.who: 1 independent checker; rebuilt both clones, regenerated OLD and NEW, own scripts (mycmp.js, mymodelreads.js, checks.js)
rounds.produced: Confirmation of the counts, lanes, byte-identity and 0 model reads; five corrections: py was runnable with real pytest (12/12), go regressed (no longer executed), 100% shared prose came partly from deleting facts, upgraded projects keep old text, the ts README contradicts itself.
rounds.changed: Its corrections became items 2, 3, 7 and 8 of brief2 (facts deleted, go program lost, upgrade keeps old text, porting one section makes a document contradict itself).

rounds.purpose: Attack the provider interface by porting two more languages (zig, clojure) and surveying the other 14.
rounds.produced: Syntax_zig and Syntax_clojure (not compiled: no toolchain), two additive interface changes (Scope.section, RuntimeWords.one), a survey of all 16 unported languages, a list of recommended interface changes, facts found in providers.
rounds.changed: Showed naming rules copied into providers (c, zig, py) and elixir's accessor needing the whole collection: brief2 item 1 and requirement A (naming hook). Recommended a call context and Scope.section, adopted in v2.

rounds.purpose: Measure whether retiring per-language components is safe for doctor, remove, target add, package update, aliases and packs (H5).
rounds.who: 1 builder, using a stand-in shared component
rounds.produced: A lifecycle change to the tool (136 added, 14 removed lines in target.ts, doctor.ts, edition.ts, remove.ts) plus a 143-line test (retire.test.ts, 7 cases), and a table of behaviours before and after across 14 rows including the language pack.
rounds.changed: Brief2 requirement E: the lifecycle change (commits a49fddc0, 7bb5161b, c193a603) is part of the build. Two hazards left open: projects with no copy record, and stale compiled output after a hand deletion.

rounds.purpose: Analyse the REFERENCE page as it is today, before building it.
rounds.produced: Block-by-block sharing counts, classes of difference, drift list, a proposed fact table per language, proposed description fields and provider additions, an H2 estimate of 2.4-2.8x.
rounds.changed: Set the shape of the shared REFERENCE page built in stage 2; its estimates were later replaced by measurements and some of its proposals proved unnecessary or wrong.

rounds.purpose: Say what stage 1 meant and what must change before more languages are ported.
rounds.produced: Eight problems from stage 1 and requirements A-F: names from the description through the code generator's own naming functions; a provider may present one complete program; runtime facts declared, structured and counted; decisions leave providers; the migration change is part of the build; count interface changes honestly.
rounds.changed: Refined the proposal: a language supplies (1) naming rules shared with its code generator and (2) printers, and does not decide what is shown.

rounds.purpose: Build interface version 2 and port a second section (the root README quick start) through the same description and providers.
rounds.produced: Naming_<lang> hooks for 6 languages, RuntimeFacts tables replacing RuntimeWords, runtimeprose.ts (sentences per result style), CallContext, Syntax.program, Expr 'fields', a runtimefacts guard test, the merged lifecycle change, an upgrade walk of a real 4.44.0 project; tutorial and root quick start for ts, go, py, c, zig, clojure.
rounds.changed: go is one program again and runs; c DOC 6/6; providers hold 0 naming rules; H2 still refuted for the two quick-start sections (1.13x on six, projected 1.75x / 1.46x).

rounds.who: 1 independent checker; rebuilt both clones, own scripts mycmp.js and mychecks.js, own lanes and own go run
rounds.produced: Confirmation of byte-identity, block counts, lanes, the go programs running, the naming claim and the upgrade walk; corrections: provider total 680 not 580, a false zig create comment, lost ts class names, an unbound clojure `entity`, a weak facts guard.
rounds.changed: Fed the stage-3 brief items 2 and 3 (sharing introduced false sentences; the guard checks names only).

rounds.purpose: Build the shared REFERENCE page on the v2 description and providers.
rounds.produced: Shared ReadmeRef.ts, DescRef and extended DescEntity, RefFacts/RefSyntax per provider, markdown.ts and media.ts; ports for ts, go, py, c, then zig; ReadmeRef_<lang> retired for those five; an extended guard; two new variations (ref-issues, no-test); fixes to the already-shared ReadmeRefFeatures; PORTING.md (205 lines).
rounds.changed: Dropped the action example after it failed lanes (ts 5/16 and py 3/12 on first run). Added RefFacts.container (a breaking change). H2 supported for this page by total lines; clojure not ported (no client type name).

rounds.purpose: Port rust and elixir completely (tutorial, root quick start, REFERENCE) and survey the remaining 12 against interface v2.
rounds.produced: Syntax and Naming for rust and elixir, three components retired in each, 5 additive interface changes, guard regexes extended for rust and elixir, a survey of 14 languages and a list of guide problems.
rounds.changed: Showed the guard's regexes know only six language families; that one section's imports serve other sections on a page (rust); recommended a declared per-family form table for the guard and several additive facts.

rounds.purpose: Independently check the shared REFERENCE page.
rounds.who: 1 independent checker; rebuilt three clones, own scripts cmp.py, prose.py, prose2.py, uniq.py, lost.py, own lanes and negative controls
rounds.produced: Confirmation of block counts, lanes, unported differences, source lines and catalogued fixes; corrections: '0 UNEXPLAINED' is structural and hid zig field types all `any`; guard checks names only; more facts lost; new defects (py `false`, `utilitys` plurals 338); README and REFERENCE contradict each other; per-language prose relocated into shared code.
rounds.changed: Fed the stage-3 brief items 1-4 and 6, 8 and the new principle (runtime notes, a per-sentence and per-block review).

rounds.purpose: Analyse the other ten README documentation families before porting them.
rounds.produced: Per-family sharing by units and by words, reaction to model switches, source lines (30,963 counted), fit per family, catalogue mapping, facts stated in several families, an after-estimate of 9,300-13,500 lines.
rounds.changed: Stage-3 brief item 9: not all documentation is the same kind of thing (Install and Explanation are documents about one language).

rounds.purpose: State what stage 2 showed and define interface version 3.
rounds.produced: A summary of stage 2 held-up and did-not-hold-up points, and a restated principle: 'The model decides what is said, once. A language supplies how its runtime spells it, and nothing a language supplies can see the model.' A language supplies naming functions, printers, declared runtime facts (enumerated where shared by two or more runtimes) and runtime notes (counted).
rounds.changed: Replaced the original sentence 'a language supplies syntax, never facts' as too strong; added a sentence ledger, per-block classification, guard coverage and cumulative interface-change counts as required measures.

findings.finding: For the quick start alone, the source does not shrink 2x. Four languages grew from 945 to 1,069 lines, and both quick-start sections in six languages went from 2,060 to 1,818 (1.13x), projecting to 1.75x over 20 languages (1.46x with c-sized providers). H2 is refuted for those sections taken alone.
findings.source: stage1.md section 1; s2-v2.txt source_lines; s2-check_v2.txt claims [7], [8]

findings.finding: Reuse across sections is real and is what makes H2 reachable. The root quick start cost 54 shared lines and 0 provider lines while retiring 2,000 lines across 20 languages. The REFERENCE page for five languages went from 2,196 to 967 lines (2.27x total, 1.89-1.92x non-blank non-comment), and all three sections together project to 2.74x across 20 languages, falling to 2.03x if providers are 1.5 times the measured size and 1.62x at twice.

Stage 1's '100% shared prose' was bought by deleting true language facts, and go's runnable program was dropped as 'structure'. When the facts were restored as declared data and go regained its program, only 69% of each language's tutorial sentences (51.6% for go) were shared by all six ported languages. That crosses H1's 15% line by sentence, even though each sentence is written once in shared code.

Naming has to be shared with the code generator, not just kept out of providers. Stage 1 reached 'zero model reads' by copying reserved-word lists and naming rules into providers; v2's per-language naming hook calls the generator's own functions and the providers then held 0 naming rules (43 hits before, 1 false positive after). It required extracting naming functions the generators did not have (py, clojure, elixir), which marks those generator files outdated in existing projects.
findings.source: stage1.md section 3; s2-v2.txt names, provider_purity, migration; s2-check_v2.txt claims [5], [6]

findings.finding: Examples still compile and run in every language with a toolchain: ts 16/16, go 12/12 (both go programs executed, exit 0), py 12/12 with real pytest, c 6/6 (up from 5/6 on old code), rust 6/6. An independent negative control proved the ts and py lanes execute REFERENCE blocks. No failure intrinsic to the approach was found; zig, clojure and elixir were never compiled, and their restructured blocks are unverified.

Sharing sentences across twenty runtimes produced a new kind of defect: one sentence drifting from many runtimes. Examples measured: zig's create comment became false, py says `ok` is `false`, C and Zig are told about a call without arguments they cannot make, and direct()'s result keys vanished in four languages. Every zig field type became `any` and was hidden by a reason-tagger that explains a line by its section.
findings.source: s2-check_v2.txt output_defects; s2-check_ref.txt output_defects and claims [0]

findings.finding: The guard over declared runtime facts is weak. It checks function names only (wrong parameters and return types passed), not nouns or type names, and its regexes know only six language families; rust failed it until extended, and for java, kotlin, csharp, php, perl, swift, cpp and ocaml it would not match the load signature at all.
findings.source: s2-check_v2.txt claims [10]; s2-check_ref.txt claims [6]; s2-probe_ref.txt guide_problems

findings.finding: Porting one section or one document at a time makes generated documentation contradict itself. In stage 1 the ts README's quick start and options table disagreed about region; after the REFERENCE port, an SDK's README and REFERENCE disagree on whether log is on by default, whether the test constructor exists, and whether region is required. Facts are stated in up to ten documentation families and must move together.
findings.source: stage1.md section 2 point 5; s2-check_ref.txt output_defects [6]-[8]; s2-restanatomy.txt facts_stated_in_several_families

findings.finding: Per-language prose was partly relocated into shared code rather than removed. Shared REFERENCE templates selected by a member kind or style that only one of the 20 runtimes declares are 29% of go's and 18% of ts's words in the part of the page each language used to write (11% and 6% of the whole page). Provider-declared words themselves are only 0.1-1.1% of the page.

Breaking interface changes stayed under H1's line of about 10. The records count about 6 since stage 1's first commit, and rust and elixir needed 5 additive and 0 breaking changes. A survey of the 12 remaining languages found none inexpressible, but 10 need an interface or fact addition and at least 8 need guard extensions; v2 and the ref round disagree on whether the naming change was breaking.

findings.finding: Catalogued issues in the ported sections are fixed once for every ported language. Independent checks found 0 instances of the quick-start issues in new output against up to 89 in old, and 17 REFERENCE checks fixed in all five ported languages. Analysis of the other README families (read, not run) estimates 24 of 105 issue ids (23%, 15% without the language pack) would still need a per-language edit.

findings.finding: Retiring per-language components is unsafe with the unmodified tool: an upgraded project silently keeps the old text and doctor reports ok. With a 136-line lifecycle change that uses the copy record, a real 4.44.0 project upgraded cleanly (12 retired copies and their compiled output removed, doctor exit 0, independently reproduced) and the language pack's output was unchanged. A component deleted by hand still runs from stale compiled output, and projects without a copy record cannot be cleaned automatically.
findings.source: stage1.md section 4; s2-v2.txt migration; s2-check_v2.txt claims [12]

findings.finding: Not all documentation is the same kind of thing. Install and Explanation have 0% of their prose shared by 15 or more languages (81% and 50% of units in one language only), and across the README families 72% of prose units but only 42% of words are shared. Much of the estimated 2.3-3.3x whole-documentation shrink is dead-code deletion (1,206 lines) and deduplication that needs no provider interface.

Restructuring examples into the shared form changes almost every block, which matters where no toolchain exists. 0 of 17-19 root quick-start blocks per language and 181-292 REFERENCE blocks per language differ from the old output. In zig, clojure and elixir those blocks were never compiled or run.
findings.source: s2-check_v2.txt claims [1]; s2-check_ref.txt claims [1]; s2-probe_ref.txt ported; brief3.md item 5

findings.finding: The principle was refined by the evidence. 'A language supplies syntax, never facts' proved too strong. By the stage-3 brief it reads: the model decides what is said, once; a language supplies naming functions shared with its code generator, printers, declared runtime facts, and counted runtime notes, and nothing a language supplies can see the model.
